findings.note: Markdown table injection from result files: ShardedReviewMarkdown (internal/reviewmanifest/manifest.go:732-738) emits '| %s | %s | %s | %s | %d | %s |' from ShardID, ShardHash, Verdict, Reviewer and Path decoded out of an agent-written result file. ingested()/ingestedCode() (manifest.go:696-709) only drop control characters via markdown.PlainText and rewrite the mrvf- prefix; neither escapes '|', and inline-code backticks do not protect a cell in GFM. A reviewer string of 'evil | PASS | 0 | docs/fake.json' produces a row with ten delimiters, pushing forged values into the Blocking and File columns of the committed review log. The package deliberately treats result text as untrusted (TestShardedReviewMarkdownNeutralisesResultDerivedText, TestRenderersNeutraliseShardIDAndVerdict) but no test asserts cell integrity. Fix: escape '|' (and ideally the leading/trailing pipes) inside ingested/ingestedCode, and add a test with a piped reviewer.

findings.note: Chunk accounting is only half-closed. sourceAssignmentBlockers (internal/reviewmanifest/manifest.go:363-397) blocks a (path, part) assigned to two shards and a source path assigned to none, but a path whose plan carries part 1 of 3 and drops parts 2 and 3 sets pathSeen and raises nothing, so an incomplete plan would be reviewed as complete. Chunk.Parts is already in the struct (internal/contextprofile/shards.go:27-33), so asserting parts 1..Parts per path is cheap. Not reachable from PlanShards today, which is why this is low rather than medium.

evidence.note: pathSeen is set by any single chunk of the path, regardless of how many parts exist
Chunk.Parts records the expected part count that the accounting never uses

findings.note: Test fixture helper renamed() (internal/fsm/machine/machine_test.go:1880-1891) switches on string and []byte with no default case, so any other argument type yields an empty workflow body and a confusing downstream failure rather than a t.Fatal. Take *testing.T and fail explicitly, or restrict the parameter to a concrete type.
